actual.descripcion: During a busy Spring Bank Holiday, the traffic cops deal with the effects of drink and drugs. A dangerous drunk driver leads traffic cops on a 20-minute chase through busy areas; a drunk driver dangerously weaves down a busy dual carriageway.

siguiente.descripcion: The Interceptors are outnumbered and outmuscled when they stop a coach load of cage fighters following an anonymous tip that there are drugs on board, and Kev and Andy pull over a Peugeot, but the occupants are in no mood to hang around.

lista.descripcion: During a busy Spring Bank Holiday, the traffic cops deal with the effects of drink and drugs. A dangerous drunk driver leads traffic cops on a 20-minute chase through busy areas; a drunk driver dangerously weaves down a busy dual carriageway.

The Interceptors are outnumbered and outmuscled when they stop a coach load of cage fighters following an anonymous tip that there are drugs on board, and Kev and Andy pull over a Peugeot, but the occupants are in no mood to hang around.

PC Damo Stevens takes on an aggressive arsonist intent on bringing Darlington to a standstill, dog handler Andy Hunt is called to a violent domestic disturbance, and Sergeant Kev Salter is hot on the heels of a runaway quad bike.

PCs Marc Crammond and Andy Clarke are on the Tyne Tunnel looking for a car on clone plates. PC Jamie Leslie is behind a car that has got his copper's nose twitching. Marc and Andy back up other units which are behind a car linked to drug dealing.
Police try to stop a suspected stolen car on the M5, two dog handlers track down a man involved in a street fight, and the hunt is on for a motorcyclist who hit an 11-year-old child.
A man observed selling drugs hides a stolen gun in a wheel well. A man admits to having a problem when used balloons and a frozen nitrous oxide tank are recovered.
A man steals his girlfriend's truck when she refuses to take him to get methadone. A woman addicted to fentanyl steals her parent's truck.
The agents may have uncovered the Cigarette-Smoking Man's true identity.

A Cornish cave rescue for Suka the terrier, the hunt for the Croydon Cat Killer, shutting down infamous puppy mills, and other pets in peril feature in a look at the threats facing animals in modern Britain.
As Australia prepares for a lockdown because of Covid-19, Steve Grahame races to beat a border shutdown. Plus, a driver battles through bush fires to get to desperate farmers.

In Northumberland, Alpha Recovery's Dave and Chris tackle two coaches that have both ended up in roadside ditches on a narrow lane. Elsewhere, Lantern's Dean and Sean attend an artic stranded by a broken wheel bearing.
In Northumberland, Kevin's winching a tanker out of a muddy ditch. His load is leaning perilously close to an ancient wall and if he gets the angle wrong, he might collapse the bricks.

Suzie Ranyard catches a man who claims that he has been driving with a dodgy number plate for the past 18 years, a rowdy reveller is apprehended on New Year's Eve in Lincoln city and Jon Moon deals with an eager shoplifter.

A father receives a reprimand for dangerous driving on the school run, a wanted man using a false identity is apprehended and during a drive to clamp down on rural crime the Interceptors pursue some stolen tractors.

Jon Moon and his dog Kanto are hot on the heels of some burglary suspects. Jason Baxter rushes to the scene of an accident where the driver was not wearing a seatbelt, only to find that another collision has taken place involving a whole line of vehicles. Finally, Jim Woolerton comes across a VW with a chassis so low that its wheels are catching on its bodywork.

Interceptor Barry outsmarts a disqualified driver, dog handler Jon takes his new sniffer dog Jack to carry out a drugs warrant, and Carl makes a jaw-dropping discovery when he pulls a car over in the early hours.

PCs Jamie Leslie and Jan Simlesa are teamed up in North Tyneside when they spot a shifty driver in a car worse for wear. In Sunderland, PC Mary-Ann Hutchison's cop car appears to spook an Audi driver into a last-minute turn and a near miss.
In Gateshead, a child is knocked off his bike, but the wait time for an ambulance is three hours. Late night, Martin spots a speedy driver. It turns out to be a takeaway emergency.
The driver of a possible cloned car refuses to come quietly to police, a woman is suspected of drug driving, and a drunk driver is remarkably jolly despite getting caught by officers.
A BMW spitting out plumes of smoke is ditched by its driver, an uninsured driver is adamant she has a policy, and police attend an unauthorised boy racer rally.
